newsitem.title: USA: CBS disputes cable industry audience study.
newsitem.headline: CBS disputes cable industry audience study.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS Inc unit on Thursday disputed the findings of a study by the cable television industry that basic cable networks grabbed as many viewers as the broadcast networks have lost this year.
CBS said its own study measuring second-quarter household audiences indicated that gains in audience by the two new broadcast networks were among the biggest.

CBS said UPN network, a unit of Chris-Craft Industries Inc allied with Viacom Inc, posted the greatest audience gains in the second quarter, adding 262,000 U.S. households compared to a year ago, while Time Warner Inc's TNT was second, gaining 258,000 households.
The WB network, a unit of Time Warner Inc, was third, adding 242,000; CBS was fourth, up 227,000; and News Corp was fifth, with 226,000.
According to CBS, both General Electric Co's NBC and Walt Disney Co's ABC sat at the bottom of the second quarter rankings of 34 networks, with the biggest audience losses for the period.
CBS criticized the cable study, saying it included too large a sample of channels, including public access and local shopping, and excluded WB and UPN. -- J. Benkoe, 212-859-1735.
